claims.text: The pinned manifest deploy/cert-manager/cert-manager.yaml (v1.20.4) creates the namespace cert-manager, six CRDs and three Deployments: cert-manager (controller), cert-manager-webhook and cert-manager-cainjector.

claims.text: Right after an install the API server may not reach cert-manager's webhook for a few seconds; cert-manager.sh's apply function retries kubectl apply 30 times, 2 s apart (about a minute).

claims.text: An Issuer is namespaced and says how Certificates in its namespace get signed; a CA Issuer (spec.ca.secretName) signs with the CA certificate and key from a Secret in the Issuer's own namespace.
claims.source_hint: cert-manager.io docs: Concepts > Issuer; Configuration > CA (secretName, same namespace as Issuer); lab-ca-issuer.yaml @ stage-3

claims.text: An Issuer can stand for a public certificate authority, which first checks that you own the name, through an HTTP URL reachable over the internet or a DNS record, so it has no way to check donhang.localhost, a name with no public owner.
claims.source_hint: cert-manager.io docs: Configuration > ACME (challenges prove control of the domain); outline item 6

claims.text: For a Certificate, cert-manager creates a private key, creates a CertificateRequest object, has it signed through the referenced Issuer and writes the result into the Secret named in spec.secretName.
claims.source_hint: cert-manager.io docs: Concepts > Certificate; Concepts > CertificateRequest

claims.text: The Secret cert-manager writes has type kubernetes.io/tls with tls.crt and tls.key; with a CA Issuer such as lab-ca it also holds ca.crt, the certificate of the signing authority (not guaranteed for other Issuers).
claims.source_hint: outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/cert-manager.txt line 17; cert-manager.io docs: Concepts > Certificate (Secret contents); Configuration > CA

claims.text: A Gateway listener reads a Secret of type kubernetes.io/tls through certificateRefs.

claims.text: Once issued, the Certificate's Ready condition is True and its status records notBefore (start of validity), notAfter (expiry), renewalTime and bookkeeping such as revision, never the certificate or key.

claims.text: At renewalTime cert-manager has a new certificate signed and writes it into the same Secret (secretName), so a reference to that Secret needs no change.
claims.source_hint: cert-manager.io docs: Concepts > Certificate > Renewal (renewBefore, renewalTime); api-certificate.yaml lines 1-6 @ stage-3

claims.text: With no duration or renewBefore in the Certificate, cert-manager's defaults give a 90-day certificate renewed 60 days after issue (two thirds of its lifetime); the lab output shows these values.
